away.headline: Jalen Hurts’ Injury: What Happened to Eagles QB? When Will NFL Star Play Again?
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles will be without quarterback Jalen Hurts for the foreseeable future amid serious injury concerns. Philadelphia has yet to announce a specific return timeline for Hurts, but there is a chance the star misses the rest of the NFL season as the quarterback continues to recover from a blood clot. Play The Eagles and Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn released a joint statement on October 19, providing a health update on the star quarterback. Hurts is expected to make a full recovery, and so far there is no reason to question whether the veteran will be able to return for the 2027 NFL season. Play Hurts may not return to the field this season, but the star remains involved in the team's offensive planning before games. Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee revealed that he is in frequent communication with Hurts prior to games. Jalen Hurts' Injury: What Happened to Eagles QB? When Will NFL Star Play Again? Unlock the latest Heavy on Eagles news — direct to your inbox. "Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season after further testing revealed deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs, following an initial diagnosis of a superficial clot in his left calf," The Athletic's Zach Berman and Brooks Kubena wrote in an October 25, story titled, "Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis: A timeline of his care and the questions that followed." "The NFL Players Association has called for a ‘full investigation' into how the NFL and the Eagles handled Hurts' medical care." Here's what you need to know about Hurts' injury. Jalen Hurts' Injury Is Deep Vein Thrombosis & the Eagles QB Is Not Expected to Play Again This Season "Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis," the joint statement revealed. "After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. "He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. ‘blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football," the statement added. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects." The NFL Will Not Punish the Eagles for the Team's Handling of Jalen Hurts' Injury Play There were conflicting reports that Hurts avoided sleeping prior to the Eagles' October 11, game in London as a result of medical advice. Hurts' agent later disputed this account. Less than one week later, Hurts was placed on injured reserve. The NFL is not expected to punish the Eagles for their handling of Hurts' injury. away.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.headline: Eagles-Commanders Final Injury Report: Saquon Barkley WILL play
home.blurb: Barkley returned to practice on Friday — albeit in a limited capacity — after being listed under did not participate on Wednesday and Thursday. There’s no question that Barkley wanting to play and help his team try to turn the season around is admirable. But the team should protect him from himself and sit him down if he’s not nearly healthy enough to play and remain in the game. Which is reasonable to think that’s the case considering he wasn’t even able to fully participate in a practice this week! While overcompensating for his hamstring injury, Barkley injured his back on his first rushing attempt in Week 7 and then played sparingly through obvious discomfort the rest of the game. What’s the point of that? What if he gets further injured? That’s not only a setback as it relates to this season, which very well might be cooked anyway, but potentially long-term as well. It could also prevent teams from making offers not only ahead of the NFL trade deadline but in the offseason, too. Even if you’re not of the mind he should be traded at any point, you should want him healthy for next year! I just think playing him is a short-sighted decision with much more downside than upside. The Eagles ruled five players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks did not practice this week ahead of their second straight game missed; the Eagles will once again be without their top two wide receivers. With Covey also out, the Eagles only have four healthy wide-outs on the roster: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. Against the Cowboys last week, Cooper played the most snaps of any Eagles WR while Lemon was right behind him. Despite this, Cooper only saw three targets while Lemon saw eight. The team will probably look to force-feed their rookie first-round pick again in this matchup. To be determined if they’ll look to elevate a fifth receiver from the practice squad. Their options there: Erik Ezukanma, Xavier Gipson (who also has returning experience), and Quentin Skinner. The Eagles ruled one player QUESTIONABLE: Jakorian Bennett. Bennett fully participated in practice all week. He’s still in his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday to activate him from IR in order for him to play on Sunday. They’ll need to open a roster spot to do so. Nolan Smith is notably set to return after missing Week 7 due to a concussion. Michael Carter II is also set to return after missing the Eagles’ last two games. Hunt and Ojomo will play but they were limited in practice all week. They’re clearly not 100%. On October 14, the Eagles opened Bennett’s 21-day practice window to return from IR. Bigsby is eligible to return to the roster after Week 8. Shipley is eligible to return to the roster after Week 9. Pierce is eligible to return to the roster after Week 12. Seattle improved its offensive line by adding All-Pro Quenton Nelson in a deal with the Indianapolis Colts while the Bears made the biggest move in trade season so far, sending two first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans as part of a package for star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons . The Bears jumped from +1400 to +1200 to win the Super Bowl after the deal, yet they remain three-point underdogs on the road in a key NFC battle on Monday. away.headline: Chicago Bears injury report is short and mostly good news for Monday night in Seattle
away.blurb: Linebackers T.J. Edwards and Jack Sanborn were both listed as full participants, while running back Kyle Monangai remained out, while two more contributors were listed as limited. T.J. Edwards has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury, and Sanborn was forced to sit out of the New England game in Week 7 due to concussion protocol. Getting both of those guys back for their trip to Seattle is not a small thing. D'Marco Jackson was listed as a limited participant due to an ankle injury, but thanks to Edwards and Sanborn returning, and the recent acquisition of Jeffrey Simmons suddenly shows that the Bears defense has depth. Muhammad was listed as limited, and with an extra day of rest, hopefully he'll be ready to go come Monday night. It's routine for teams to conduct this virtual walkthrough on a day where the team doesn't hold physical practice. The linebacker room is whole again Seattle wants to run and be the more physical team , and Chicago's defense has been stretched thin for weeks. Their performance against New England was encouraging, but the defense is a much better unit when everyone is healthy. Kyle Monangai is the sole Bears player who didn't participate. simultaneously dealing with a thumb and a turf toe injury that's kept him on the sidelines since Week 4 against the Jets, following his 30 carry, 146 yard, two touchdown performance. Chicago's run game still has D'Andre Swift, but the Ben Johnson system functions best with two excellent running backs at the team's disposal. Roschon Johnson has stepped up to fill the gap, but the recent signing of Zavier Scott to the practice squad, followed by his immediate promotion to the active roster suggests that the Bears aren't fully on-board with him in the backfield. Until Monangai returns, it appears that Johnson and Scott will be alternating touches. The last player on the list is third round rookie, Malik Muhammad. The thumb issue looked minor. The toe injury was a different story. Cole Kmet Update: Why Bears $50 Million TE Won't Catch Another Pass in 2026 Kyle Monangai Turf Toe Recovery Timeline Turf toe is a sprain of the ligaments and joint capsule at the base of the big toe, the joint a running back relies on to push off, accelerate and cut. Recovery runs on a sliding scale. A Grade 1 stretch heals in days to two weeks , a Grade 2 partial tear takes two to eight weeks, and a Grade 3 complete tear can sideline a player for six to 12 weeks or more, sometimes requiring surgery. Those ranges are general medical guidance, not a diagnosis of Monangai. Four weeks and three missed games fit the Grade 2 range. That timeline is typical for an injury that required a specialist and a boot, while milder sprains resolve faster and higher-graded ones linger longer. Chicago has kept Monangai off IR, which requires a minimum four-game absence, because the team expected a shorter timeline. Johnson has called him week-to-week and "trending in the right direction," he said, according to Sports Illustrated .
